vendor_build._note: Runs ONLINE in the vendor stage, before go mod vendor, so its outputs are part of the vendored tree the offline stage rebuilds from. (1) go-swagger v0.33.1 generates src/server/v2.0/{models,restapi} from api/v2.0/swagger.yaml with Harbor's templates - the exact `make gen_apis` command; those packages are NOT committed and core does not compile without them. (2) The portal: make/photon/portal/Dockerfile's recipe run in-tree (src/portal/.nvmrc = v22.22.3, so node_version 22), then dist + swagger.json + the swagger-ui bundle are collected into readystack-portal/ and node_modules are deleted (the renderer only removes a top-level node_modules). (3) The registry: goharbor/distribution v2.8.3-harbor.3 (Makefile REGISTRY_SRC_TAG / DISTRIBUTION_SRC) cloned to third_party/distribution; it has its own go.mod (module github.com/docker/distribution, go 1.27.2) and becomes the second multi_module dir. generate-build-timestamp writes the build time into the portal bundle; that happens once, online, and the offline rebuild copies the vendored bundle, so the offline digest is unaffected.

binaries_from_source._note: Makefile CORE_LDFLAGS (GITCOMMIT = 8-char short sha, RELEASEVERSION = VERSION file = v2.15.4). `-h` exits 0 at flag.Parse before any config or network (main.go: only the PPROF_ENABLED-gated pprof starts first).

binaries_from_source.name: harbor_jobservice
binaries_from_source._note: jobservice loads its configuration from core over REST BEFORE flag.Parse (main.go: cfgLib.DefaultMgr().Load), so `-h` panics without a running core. The verify therefore only proves the binary was produced: a failed go build skips the -h (&&) and test -x then fails the stage.

Revision is the commit of v2.8.3-harbor.3. version.Version is deliberately NOT stamped: scripts/retarget.py tokenizes any `Version=vX.Y` in ldflags into @VERSION_BARE@ (Harbor's version), which would mislabel the registry; it reports its source default v2.8.3+unknown plus this revision.
